evidence: Nearly all the weight is Marcos Cezar de Freitas: Historiografia brasileira em perspectiva (23), História social da infância no Brasil (6), Os intelectuais na história da infância (4), and the education/historiography titles. Charles Frederick Hartt (2) is an isolated work by Marcus Vinicius de Freitas; the display name is wrong for the dominant works.

The two 1832 Diccionario da Lingua Brasileira entries account for 31 of 50 listed citation counts and are by Luiz Maria da Silva Pinto. Costa Pinto wrote O negro no Rio de Janeiro (9) and both Lutas de Famílias entries (4 combined); even allowing the short Sociologia and UNESCO entries, his share is about 15/50.

Luiz Gonçalves dos Santos wrote the two Memórias para servir entries (12 combined) and Réplica Católica (1), about 13/42. O pensamento sanitário/sanitarista (5 combined) is by Luiz Antonio de Castro Santos; the 1985 Dados fragment (9) likely represents that article. The later health writings also belong to Castro Santos, not Padre Perereca.

Memórias da Rua do Ouvidor (11), Um passeio pela cidade do Rio de Janeiro (7), both Anno/Ano Biográfico entries (11 combined), As vítimas-algozes (5), the Lições de História do Brasil editions and Mulheres de Mantilha are Joaquim Manuel de Macedo's works. Manoel/Manuel and the honorific Dr. do not indicate another author; the tiny incomplete entries remain uncertain.

Nearly all the weight is the nineteenth-century José Martiniano de Alencar: Como e porque sou romancista, O sertanejo, O Guarani, O Demônio familiar, Ao correr da pena, Senhora, A propriedade, Erasmo's political letters, Systema Representativo, Mãe and Iracema. The 2002 Joaquim Nabuco compilation (1) is associated with José Almino de Alencar; the journal-only entry is unresolved.

Roberto Cardoso de Oliveira's Identidade, etnia e estrutura social (11), A crise do indigenismo (3), O índio e o mundo dos brancos (3), Caminhos da identidade (3), Do índio ao bugre (2), O trabalho do antropólogo (2) and related identity texts supply roughly three quarters of the weight. Periferia com o poder da palavra (2) is Roberto Camargos's thesis; Sindicalismo e democracia is Roberto Véras's, and Campo e ação das identificações is Roberto Menezes's. Journal-only fragments are uncertain.

Dos cortiços aos condomínios fechados (6) and Cidade, povo e nação (3) are Luiz Cesar de Queiroz Ribeiro's; the 1996 Civilização Brasileira fragment (4) probably refers to the latter, with two further urban-segregation entries bringing his likely weight to about 15/32. Ofício criador (3), O comércio e a navegação (3), Excelsos Destinos (2) and Modos de ver (2) belong to Luiz Cláudio Ribeiro. The bare '(org)' and other fragments remain unresolved.

Edward John Thompson wrote The Making of the Indian Princes, Rise and Fulfilment of British Rule in India and the Metcalfe biography (16 citation counts across their variants), plus Sir Walter Raleigh and Burmese Silver, about 18/41. The two 1967 Past and Present fragments (18 combined) likely stand for Edward Palmer Thompson's Time, Work-Discipline, and Industrial Capitalism; The Grid of Inheritance (2) is also E. P. Thompson's. Thus the LC author is a substantial minority.

Geografia histórica da Capitania de Minas Gerais (14/35) is the eighteenth-century cartographer José Joaquim da Rocha's work. Roberto Silveira: a pedra e o fogo (3) is by José Sérgio Rocha, the Vasco da Gama history (3) by José da Silva Rocha, and Teologia & Negritude (3) by José Geraldo da Rocha. The twentieth-century infant-care works cannot be the LC person's; the Revista do Arquivo Público Mineiro fragment (2) is unresolved.

Paulo Ferreira Santos wrote Formação de cidades no Brasil colonial (6) and Subsídios para o estudo da arquitetura religiosa em Ouro Preto (4), and contributed the study in O álbum da Avenida Central (2): about 12/30. Músico, doce músico (3) is Paulo Sérgio Malheiros dos Santos's, while Entre o laboratório, o campo e outros lugares (2) is Paulo Roberto Elian dos Santos's. Other modern political, labor and exhibition-history titles add further pooled works.
